_what_this_is: One entry per closed optimisation loop on a noise experiment. A loop is measured, changed ONE thing, re-measured. An entry without both a before and an after number is not a loop and does not belong here. Read by coverage.py.

_fields.dataset: the dataset it was measured on, and how many molecules
_fields.changed: the one thing that changed, in words
_fields.before: the number before, with its unit named
_fields.after: the number after, with its unit named
_fields.kept: true if the change stayed in the file, false if it was reverted
_fields.note: optional: what the number does not settle

loops.dataset: flab_thermo_tresanco, 672 antibodies, 448 per training fold, saprot, random forest, spearman
loops.changed: how far a label moves toward its target, from the alpha of 0.5 that oof_smooth and gp_smooth run at to an alpha of 1.0, with the suspicion score rescaled the same way in both
loops.before: aiming at a Gaussian-process posterior mean, 0.4509 spearman; aiming at a LightGBM out-of-fold prediction, 0.4581 spearman; aiming at the mean label of the ten nearest molecules, 0.4331 spearman
loops.after: aiming at a Gaussian-process posterior mean, 0.4996 spearman; aiming at a LightGBM out-of-fold prediction, 0.4703 spearman; aiming at the mean label of the ten nearest molecules, 0.4552 spearman
loops.note: Three folds, one noise draw each, injected level 2.0, one molecule in ten given the wide error. Clean 0.5985 spearman, corrupted 0.4111, so the gap is 0.1874 spearman. The mean of three folds moves the right way for all three targets, but FOLD BY FOLD it is 7 of 9 paired readings, not 9: on the third fold moving the whole way LOST for the LightGBM target (0.4262 down to 0.3866 spearman) and for the neighbour mean (0.4076 down to 0.3951). Only the Gaussian-process target won on all three folds. The best single setting is gp_smooth moving the whole way, 0.4996 spearman and 47.2 percent of the gap, against 0.4509 and 21.2 percent at the half-way setting it runs at -- so the two model-based corrections coming last of seven in the completed run is the ranking of one alpha, not of the targets. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE: for the neighbour-mean target, overwriting the flagged tenth outright scored 0.4829 spearman against 0.4552 for moving every label the whole way, so knn_smooth's shape is not beaten. And rescaling the suspicion score by its rank put the labels closest to clean on all three folds -- 7.12 to 7.69 label units against 10.85 to 12.95 for every other setting -- while recovering the least of the gap, so the correction that repairs the most labels is not the one that recovers the most score. NOT APPLIED: one dataset, one representation, one downstream model, one dose, and n18 already sweeps this same alpha over 0.25, 0.5 and 1.0 for exactly these two cleanups. WHY IT MOVES AT ALL: the Outlier condition is Huber contamination at lambda 3, so every training label carries an error and the flagged tenth carries one about three times wider -- 39.32 label units from clean on the 39 molecules flagged in fold 0 against 12.67 on the other 409, clean label standard deviation 10.12. Run cost 5999 seconds for the three folds on a machine at load 200 to 480.

loops.dataset: flab_thermo_tresanco, 672 antibodies, saprot, 3 scaffold-grouped folds, 1 corruption draw each, injected level 2.0, one molecule in ten corrupted
loops.changed: the fraction of the way a score-proportional correction moves a label, from 0.5 to 1.0, holding the correction's target fixed
loops.before: share of the 0.1874 spearman clean-to-corrupted gap recovered at 0.5: 21.2% for the gaussian-process target, 11.7% for the neighbour mean, 25.0% for the out-of-fold prediction
loops.after: at 1.0: 47.2%, 23.5% and 31.6% for the same three targets
loops.note: COMPLETE at 3 folds, 5999 seconds. Clean 0.5985 spearman against corrupted 0.4111. NOT applied: the correction strength is n18's axis to settle and n18 measured the opposite on real labels, so the default is not this loop's to move. Recorded because it refutes the reading that the min-max rescale was what held these corrections back. Replacing the raw score with its rank at the same 1.0, which makes that rescale the identity, LOST at all three targets: 19.4%, 9.4% and 13.3%. ⛔ CORRECTED 2026-09-21: this entry said both comparisons held at 3 of 3 targets on every one of the three passes. They do not. The partial tables the probe prints are CUMULATIVE means over the passes so far, not per-pass values, and reading them as per-pass is what produced that claim. Recovering each pass from the cumulative means: moving the whole way beat moving half way in 7 of 9 paired readings, losing on the third fold for the out-of-fold target (0.4262 down to 0.3866 spearman) and for the neighbour mean (0.4076 down to 0.3951). The raw score beat its rank in 8 of 9, losing on the second fold for the neighbour mean (0.4963 against 0.4881). Only the gaussian-process target won both comparisons on all three folds. The three-fold MEANS still move the way this entry reports. ⛔ DUPLICATE: this is the same measurement as the entry whose `changed` begins "how far a label moves toward its target"; one run, two rows, so the table counts it twice. The TARGET matters less than one pass suggested: the gaussian process leads at 47.2% but the neighbour mean's best shape is 'replace' at 38.3%, which read 11.0% after one pass and 26.2% after two, so that cell is not settled. Separately, the shape that moved labels closest to their clean values was not the shape that scored best -- rank at 1.0 cut the mean distance from a corrupted training label to its clean value from 14.94 label units to between 7.12 and 7.69 and still lost the held-out spearman to proportional at 1.0, which reached only 10.85 to 11.03 units. The gaussian process ran without importance-weighted kernel inputs. ⛔ n18 measured the SAME axis on labels nobody corrupted and found alpha 1.0 LOSES at every correction: label_smooth best at 0.25, oof_smooth and gp_smooth best at 0.5, downweight best at a 4-to-1 row weight ratio. The two experiments ask different questions -- share of an injected gap recovered, against held-out spearman on real labels -- and which one sets the default is an open decision.

loops.dataset: flab_thermo_tresanco, 672 antibodies, 448 in fold 0's training block, saprot, 1280 features
loops.changed: weighted the Gaussian process's kernel inputs by each feature's lightgbm gain, which is what cut a Gaussian process's error by 29 percent in n21
loops.before: the posterior mean gp_smooth aims every label at spans 1.6899 label units across the 448 molecules and rank-correlates with the labels it was fitted on at -0.0234 spearman
loops.after: the same 1.6899 label units and the same -0.0234 spearman; the two posterior means differ by 0.00000000 label units, bit-identical
loops.note: THE WEIGHTING IS NOT THE FINDING. It reached the kernel and it was drastic -- lightgbm gives gain to only 361 of saprot's 1280 features, so 919 columns were multiplied by zero and both guards in GaussianProcessEstimator passed. Nothing changed because the process is not reading its inputs. Counted directly: the 448 molecules receive 3 DISTINCT posterior-mean values, 64.0567, 65.7113 and 65.7467 label units, and each is exactly the mean label of the inner fold that molecule was held out of -- inner fold 0 trains on 298 molecules whose mean label is 64.0567 and every molecule it held out received 64.0567. The fitted noise level is 22.7930 label units against a fitted-label standard deviation of 22.8228, so the process assigns all of the variance to noise and its posterior mean is its prior mean. So gp_smooth does not move a label toward what a Gaussian process predicts for that molecule, which is what n07's docstring says it does; it moves every label toward the mean label of its inner fold. It is shrinkage toward the mean under a model's name. This is one representation at 1280 features over 448 molecules, which is the regime where an isotropic RBF kernel flattens because every pair of molecules is nearly the same distance apart; whether a narrower feature set revives it is not measured.

loops.dataset: flab_thermo_tresanco, 672 antibodies, saprot, 448 in the training fold, 1280 features, injected level 2.0, one molecule in ten corrupted
loops.changed: the gaussian process that gp_smooth corrects toward had its kernel inputs multiplied by feature importance, instead of left unweighted
loops.before: share of the 0.2538 spearman clean-to-corrupted gap recovered, unweighted: 28.4% moving a label a quarter of the way, 47.5% all the way, 41.3% by rank, 31.1% replacing outright
loops.after: identical to four decimal places at all four shapes: 28.4%, 47.5%, 41.3%, 31.1%
loops.note: ⛔ NOT a null result about weighting. The gaussian process is DEGENERATE at the width n07 fits it at, so there is nothing for a weighting to change. Fitted on all 1280 features it returned 3 distinct posterior-mean values across 448 training molecules -- one constant per inner fold, nothing read from the features -- and the same at the 361 features lightgbm gives any gain. It starts fitting between 361 features and 200: at 200 it returns 226 distinct values and beats the corrupted labels by 0.3303 spearman against -0.0441 at 1280. This is the likely reason gp_smooth ranked second from bottom of the seven corrections at 13.4% -- it was smoothing toward a constant. At 200 features the weighting LOSES, 0.2709 against 0.3303 spearman, one fold only. The width has to be fixed before the weighting question can be asked, and the 29% gain measured for the similarity work is not contradicted by this -- it was measured where the process was actually fitting.

loops.dataset: flab_thermo_tresanco, 672 antibodies, 448 in fold 0's training block, saprot, 1280 features, injected level 2.0 of the clean label standard deviation, one molecule in ten given the wide error
loops.changed: the RBF kernel's length scale starts at the median distance between the training molecules it is fitted on, instead of at 1.0, in GaussianProcessEstimator.estimate (src/kirby/utils/noise_estimation.py)
loops.before: the posterior mean gp_smooth aims every label at took 3 distinct values across the 448 molecules, rank-correlated with the CLEAN labels at -0.0441 spearman, and sat 11.0137 label units from the clean label of the 39 molecules the injector gave the wide error
loops.after: 358 distinct values across the same 448 molecules, 0.5630 spearman against the clean labels, and 9.5756 label units from those 39 molecules' clean labels
loops.note: THE MECHANISM, not a tuning choice. An RBF kernel is exp(-d^2 / 2l^2). Two standardised molecules described by saprot's 1280 features sit about sqrt(2 * 1280) = 50.6 apart, so at a length scale of 1.0 every off-diagonal entry of the kernel matrix underflows, the matrix is the identity and the marginal likelihood is flat in the length scale. Recorded per inner fold: the three fitted length scales came back 1.01, 1.00 and 1.01, having never left the start, and the white-noise level pinned at 1.0, its own upper bound. After the change they are 61.87, 54.26 and 41.85 with noise levels 0.8884, 0.8328 and 0.8446. sklearn's n_restarts_optimizer=3 does not rescue it because each restart is sampled log-uniformly across the length-scale bounds, which were (1e-5, 1e5) -- ten orders of magnitude -- so a restart almost never lands near the data's own distance; the bounds are now a factor of 100 either side of the start. NARROWING THE FEATURE SET IS NO LONGER NEEDED: at 1280 features the fixed start reaches 0.5630 spearman against the clean labels, beating every narrowed width measured against the broken start (0.3303 at 200 features, 0.2473 at 50, 0.4360 at 5). At 200 features the fixed start reaches 0.6014, so width still buys something, and at 5 features the two starts agree to four decimals (0.4360 both) because a median distance of about 3 and a start of 1.0 are close enough. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE: one fold, one noise draw, one dataset, one representation. This is the TARGET's quality, not a recovery figure -- what it does to the share of the clean-to-corrupted gap gp_smooth puts back is the next measurement. It also changes every other caller of GaussianProcessEstimator: n07's own 'gaussian_process' detector and n11's gp target and detector. Neither was re-measured here. The same median heuristic was already in this file's heteroscedastic Gaussian process (torch.cdist(...).median()).
